radiopost_vectors: Forwarding: placements, session records, and the post office's side
rule: A placement made from `placement_body` with radiopost.org's key is exactly `placement_hex`; a gateway checking a placement case with `me` and `now`, and the post office keys of keys.json, returns `expect` (RP-7 §4.3). A record's ID is SHA-256 of its statement, cut to 12 bytes (RP-7 §3.1). A partner (`me`) holding the credentials `held_hex` and checking a PROOF case from `caller` returns `expect` (RP-7 §3.2, §3.3). A station of `country` may publish or call in a window whose signal occupies `occupied_hz` when `expect` is true (RP-7 §5, §5.1). A cut-off gateway in `calling`'s window at `now`, knowing `partners`, sends it its records when `expect` is true (RP-7 §5, §6.2). The post office's exchanges read as in api-exchanges.json.

post_office.note: N2CALL-5 polls for copies, as it does all the time, and takes the copy of #421.

Atlanta loses the Internet. N2CALL-5 polls no more; 15 minutes on, radiopost.org counts it cut off (RP-7 §4.1). Shelter 3 and Facundo call N2CALL-5, which checks them offline and keeps their session records (RP-7 §3.1).
Shelter 3 named N2CALL-5 as usual, and N2CALL-5 is cut off: the route sends the mail to N1CALL-10, as a forward item with a placement signed by radiopost.org (RP-7 §4.2).

In N1CALL-10's window N2CALL-5 calls it (session-04.json): the two records go out, the forward item comes in. N1CALL-10 reaches radiopost.org and reports the records with their path (RP-5 §5.6, RP-7 §3.4).
A report whose path does not end at the reporting gateway is refused (RP-5 §5.6).

Atlanta's Internet returns. N2CALL-5's poll ends the forwarding: radiopost.org has the forward item at N1CALL-10 dropped (RP-7 §4.1). N2CALL-5 gets the copy of #501 it already holds by radio; the copy of #421, picked up, is dropped.
